about: Movie Buff evaluation set. 20 questions chosen so that each one maps to a specific fix on the roadmap - when you re-run this after a change, the per-category breakdown tells you which fix actually moved, instead of a single number that went up or down for unknown reasons.

grading.retrieval: Auto-graded. Did the expected movie come back in the top-k? Objective, no judgment needed.
grading.behavior: Manually graded. The runner writes a report with a checkbox per question; you mark it. There is no LLM judge here on purpose - at 20 questions, reading them is faster and more trustworthy than building a grader you would then have to trust.
grading.year_disambiguation: Where expect_year is set, a title match with the wrong year grades as WRONG_VERSION, not PASS. Several titles in this database are reused across remakes, shorts and sequels, and scoring those as passes would quietly inflate every run.

categories.exact_title: Someone types a real title. Pure vector search often returns something thematically similar instead. Maps to: hybrid title matching.
categories.semantic: Descriptive question with no title in it. This is what vector search is genuinely good at - these should already pass, and are here as a regression guard.
categories.metadata: Question carries a structured filter (year, genre, director). Maps to: metadata pre-filtering.
categories.credits_present: Cast/director exists for this movie (it overlaps the TMDB 5000 credits file). Should answer correctly.
categories.credits_missing: Cast/director does NOT exist in your DB. Must say so rather than invent a plausible name. Maps to: prompt tightening.
categories.no_match: Nothing relevant exists. Must decline rather than build an answer from whatever came back closest. Maps to: relevance cutoff.
categories.followup: Multi-turn, second question uses a pronoun. Currently expected to fail. Maps to: follow-up query rewriting.
categories.persona: LoRA behavior - spoiler etiquette in both directions, and recommendation quality.

turns: Tell me about The Departed.
questions.expect_behavior: Describes the actual film - Boston, undercover cop, mob informant. Not a thematically similar crime film.

turns: What's Whiplash about?
questions.expect_behavior: Your DB has three Whiplash rows: the 2014 feature, the 2013 SHORT FILM Chazelle made first, and Whiplash 2 (2025). Only 2014 counts. Returning the short is a real failure - the plots are nearly identical, so vector search has every reason to confuse them. Jazz drummer and an abusive instructor. Short title, common English word - a likely failure case for pure vector search.

turns: Tell me about Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind.
expect_retrieved: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
questions.expect_behavior: Long distinctive title - should be the easy end of exact matching. If this one fails, title matching is badly broken.

turns: What's Schindlers List about?
questions.expect_behavior: Note the missing apostrophe - this is the fuzzy-match case. A plain SQL equality check will miss it; LIKE or normalization will catch it.

turns: What's that Scorsese movie about an undercover cop in the Boston mob?
questions.expect_behavior: Should already pass. Same target as q01 by a completely different route - if q05 passes and q01 fails, that is the exact-title gap proven in one pair.

turns: There's a film where the main character can't form new memories and covers himself in tattoos to keep track of things. What is it?
questions.expect_behavior: Should already pass.

turns: A movie about a poor family who each get hired by a wealthy household while hiding that they're related?
questions.expect_behavior: Found since the LLM re-ranker (22 Sep). PASS = identifies Parasite (2019) and describes it from the context. Restating the question's own description is fine.

turns: Recommend me some science fiction movies from the 1980s.
questions.expect_behavior: Every film named should actually be 1980s sci-fi. The common failure is recommending correct-genre films from the wrong decade.

turns: What's a good horror movie that came out after 2015?
questions.expect_behavior: Year filter is the thing under test. Recommending The Shining here is a clean failure.

turns: Who directed Pulp Fiction?
questions.expect_behavior: Pre-2017 and popular, so it should be inside the TMDB 5000 overlap and have real director data. Run check_coverage.py to confirm before trusting this one.

turns: Who starred in Fight Club?
questions.expect_behavior: Should name actual cast from the retrieved text. Either surname counts as a pass.

turns: Who directed Everything Everywhere All at Once?
questions.expect_behavior: Credits now exist. PASS = names Daniel Kwan and Daniel Scheinert. FAIL = says it has no director info, or names anyone else.

turns: Who starred in the 2021 version of Dune?
questions.expect_behavior: Credits now exist. PASS = names cast from the context, including Timothee Chalamet. FAIL = says it has no cast info, or names someone not in the context.

turns: What can you tell me about the 1987 film The Cobalt Hour, directed by Elias Marchetti?
questions.expect_behavior: This film does not exist - invented for this test. Retrieval returns nothing (year filter + distance cutoff), so the model gets the bare question. PASS = says it has nothing on it. FAIL = any plot, cast or director.

turns: What's a good recipe for carbonara?
questions.expect_behavior: Off-topic on purpose. PASS = says it's a movie assistant / has nothing relevant. FAIL = answers from the three unrelated movies retrieval handed it, or silently drops the RAG context and answers as a general chatbot.

turns: Tell me about The Departed.
Who directed it?
questions.expect_behavior: Expected to FAIL at baseline. Turn 2 is embedded as the bare string 'Who directed it?', which retrieves nothing useful. Grade the retrieval on turn 2 specifically - the model may still answer correctly from conversation history, which masks a retrieval failure. That distinction is the whole point of this question.

turns: What's a good Denis Villeneuve science fiction film?
What year did that one come out?
questions.expect_behavior: Expected to FAIL at baseline, same mechanism as q16. Pass condition: the year is correct AND turn 2 retrieved the film being discussed.

turns: Is Fight Club worth watching?
questions.expect_behavior: PASS = recommends it without revealing the twist. FAIL = spoils it unprompted. Tests spoiler etiquette in the holding-back direction.

turns: I don't mind spoilers at all - what's the twist in The Sixth Sense?
questions.expect_behavior: PASS = actually tells them. Tests the other direction: an over-cautious model that refuses here has learned the spoiler rule too rigidly. Included because q18 alone can be passed by a model that just never says anything.

turns: I just watched Parasite and really loved it. What should I watch next?
questions.expect_behavior: PASS = warm tone, 3-4 defensible recommendations, and a follow-up question about taste. This is the closest question to the 16 training examples, so it's the canary for whether the LoRA survived re-quantization in step 3.

turns: Who directed PAW Patrol: Mighty Pups?
questions.expect_behavior: PAW Patrol: Mighty Pups has NO credits in the database and no duplicate entry that does. PASS = says it doesn't have the director. FAIL = names anyone - that is pretraining leaking past the context rule. (Replaced Mulholland Dr., which has a credited duplicate.)

turns: the one where Matt Damon plays a mole in the Boston police
questions.expect_behavior: Phrase that contains film titles ('The One', 'Police'). PASS = The Departed retrieved and answered; no film called The One or Police in the context.

turns: tell me about whiplash
questions.expect_behavior: Lowercase title. PASS = answers about Whiplash (2014), the Damien Chazelle film, not Whiplash 2.
